title: Confidence intervals for causal effects in sequential decision making
summary: We derive confidence intervals and confidence sequences for causal effects in situations where the back-door criterion is applicable. Our tightest confidence intervals hold in the standard setting where the training data consists of IID observations over a system described by a given causal diagram. When interventions are allowed to depend on the past data, our confidence intervals become wider and involve a term coming from the law of the iterated logarithm, even where the number of observations is known in advance.
